text: just seen my flatmate weighing pasta at 11pm. no barcode. no photo. no cal ai. just kitchen scales and a notes app with three years of half finished entries. stood there scrolling a food database for nine minutes while the pasta went cold. she's built different and wrong

audio: original audio, room tone, fork on bowl
caption: the pasta was cold. the entry was still wrong

text: i logged a mixed curry by vibes on saturday. no label. no barcode. no cal ai. just me under the table googling how many calories in chicken tikka while my food went cold. typed in 1200. added a bit for the naan. closed the app. brave. stupid. brave.

text: watched a lad ask chatgpt how many calories in his mum's lasagne. described the whole dish. portion size. type of mince. no scales. no cal ai. no label. then argued with it when it said 900. sat there negotiating with a robot over lasagne. genuinely unwell

text: i bulked for four months with a paper food diary in my gym bag. no scan. no barcode. no cal ai. just measuring cups and a biro that ran out in week two. wrote down big rice twice a day and called it tracking. hit my protein by faith alone. respect to past me. barely
base_video: Creator sat on a bench in a gym changing room or bedroom floor, gym bag open beside them, holding a battered notebook, flicking a page and giving the camera a slow blink.
caption: big rice. that was the entry. that was it
why_this_brand: A paper diary, measuring cups and a made up portion size is the pre-app bulking method Cal AI's macro tracking replaces.
